pos.m: 使某人產生防衛心，使某人覺得受威脅

ex.en: The phrase to put someone on the defensive means to do or say something which makes them feel threatened or unsure.
ex.zh: 「to put someone on the defensive」這個片語的意思是，做或說了某件事，讓對方覺得受到威脅或不確定。

tips.t: be on the defensive 處於防守狀態；defensive 形容詞「防衛的」（國際學村 Day 02 滿分字）：Try not to become defensive when receiving feedback.

ex.en: These emails are examples of people being uncivil – an adjective meaning rude or impolite.
ex.zh: 這些信都是有人 uncivil 的例子——這個形容詞的意思是粗魯或不禮貌。

fam: civil adj. 有禮貌的；民事的

tips.t: civil 另一個常見意思是「民事的、公民的」：civil engineer 土木工程師、civil servant 公務員。workplace incivility 職場無禮，是人資常見議題。

ex.en: Last year, thousands of US government workers received an email requiring them to justify their job by listing five things they had accomplished that week...
ex.zh: 去年，數千名美國政府員工收到一封電子郵件，要求他們列出當週完成的五件事，來證明自己的工作有存在的必要……

fam: justifiable adj. 正當的，合理的

tips.t: justify the cost / expense 說明費用的正當性；Can you justify this decision? 你能說明這個決定的理由嗎？預算、採購情境常見。

ex.en: Emails that are hostile in tone and language, or even cc'ing senior personnel in on the message in order to elevate an issue and put someone in their place.
ex.zh: 像是語氣和用字充滿敵意的信，甚至把資深人員加進副本，好把事情升級、讓對方知道自己的分量。

tips.t: personnel（人員，重音在最後）≠ personal（個人的，重音在第一音節）。authorized personnel only 閒人勿進；personnel department 人事部。

forms.note: 集合名詞（通常當複數用）

der: personal adj. 個人的（易混淆）

ex.en: The fight response can make us belittle someone – make them feel inferior or unimportant.
ex.zh: 「戰」的反應可能讓我們貶低別人——讓對方覺得自己低人一等或不重要。

tips.t: 同義：look down on、undermine。職場霸凌相關文件常見：belittling remarks 貶低人的言論。

pos.m: 功勞，讚揚；信用；（帳戶）存款

ex.en: For example, a boss sends a group email in which they give someone else the credit for the work you did.
ex.zh: 例如，主管寄了一封群組信，把你做的工作功勞歸給別人。

tips.t: 一字多義必考：take credit for 把功勞攬在自己身上；credit card 信用卡；store credit 購物金；The refund will be credited to your account. 退款將存入您的帳戶。

pos.m: 把事情從自己手上移走（交給別人處理）

ex.en: Such colleagues want to get work off their plate – another idiom, meaning to remove tasks from your own workload and give them to someone else to deal with.
ex.zh: 這樣的同事想 get work off their plate——這是另一個慣用語，意思是把工作從自己的工作量中移走，丟給別人處理。

tips.t: 相關：have a lot on one's plate 手上事情很多（I have a lot on my plate this week. 我這週很忙）。workload 工作量，多益常見。

pos.m: 疲憊不堪的，心力交瘁的

ex.en: We're more likely to be uncivil when we're frazzled – an informal adjective describing feeling tired or anxious because you're doing too many things at the same time.
ex.zh: 我們 frazzled 時更容易無禮——這個非正式的形容詞，形容因為同時做太多事而感到疲憊或焦慮。

tips.t: 口語說法，正式文章常用 exhausted、overwhelmed、burned out（職業倦怠）。
